insights.summary: FY26 consolidated revenue rose 23% to ₹830 Cr on 33% higher volumes, with EBITDA margin up to 17.4%, but interest and depreciation from the new Pakhajan plant kept standalone PAT at only ₹21 Cr. Management targets over 75% utilisation and an EBITDA margin of ~20% in FY27, 35-45% volume growth, and ₹1,500 Cr of revenue in FY28 when a 15-year contract with an MNC (₹51.4 Cr advance received) starts. Capex of ₹125 Cr is planned from internal accruals while debt/EBITDA falls from 3.75x toward 2.5x.

what_changed.text: 15-year MNC supply agreement; ₹51.4 Cr advance; revenue from FY28
FY27 capex ₹125 Cr at Pakhajan, internally funded

tone.label: steady
tone.quote: Let me be honest. Neither I have a crystal ball nor I have a source from a White House, which can give you that information, what's going to happen tomorrow.

analyst_questions.answer: Expect 2-3 points higher EBITDA as utilisation passes 70%, i.e. ~20%.
High stock helped through the supply crisis; aim for 170-175 days in 6-12 months.
Not a threat for 10-15 years; industrial lubricants (data centres, wind) growing.

red_flags.text: Debt ~₹558 Cr and debt/EBITDA 3.75x; interest ate most of FY26 operating profit.
Raw-material delays (8-12 weeks) and shipping to the US now 60-70 days.
Only ~40% of revenue on contracted pricing; 60% spot.

watch_next: Utilisation and volume growth in Q1
Progress on the MNC contract plant
Price increases (10-15%) passed through from April

business_snapshot.what_they_make: Specialty chemicals: lubricant additives, rubber chemicals (antioxidants), other industrial chemicals, and food and aroma chemicals
business_snapshot.customers: Global lubricant-additive and rubber majors and MNC formulators; ~600 customers; top customer ~7% of revenue
business_snapshot.demand_drivers: Supply-chain diversification from China, industrial lubricants, rubber and tyre demand, long-term MNC contracts
